context_length: Single sequence in this benchmark; E1 can also take retrieved homologs as context
summary: The 300M Profluent E1 encoder: a retrieval-augmented protein LM designed as a drop-in replacement for ESM models. Here it is used on single sequences, producing 1024-dim embeddings.
architecture: Encoder-only transformer, 20 layers and hidden size 1024, with attention within each sequence and a global layer across sequences every third layer. Run here on single sequences.
pretraining_data: About 4 trillion tokens from the Profluent Protein Atlas.
pretraining_objective: Masked language modeling with retrieved homologous sequences in the context, read through block-causal multi-sequence attention; the released models also run on a single sequence.
key_innovations: Retrieval augmentation: conditions on homologous sequences through block-causal multi-sequence attention
Reported state-of-the-art zero-shot fitness and unsupervised contact prediction; designed as a drop-in replacement for ESM models
when_to_use: As a modern ESM-style encoder; its retrieval augmentation is not used here, since the benchmark embeds single sequences.
caveats: 2025 preprint. It was designed to condition on retrieved homologs, which this benchmark does not supply. Weights under the Profluent-E1 license, which allows research and commercial use with attribution.

citations.authors: Jain, S., Beazer, J., Ruffolo, J. A., Bhatnagar, A., Madani, A.
citations.title: E1: Retrieval-Augmented Protein Encoder Models
